gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 19?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from agencies including the UK Met Office center Munich’s August 19 maximum near 28–30 °C under mostly sunny skies, light westerly flow, and modest daytime heating that favors peak readings in this narrow band. Trader consensus, reflected in the 44 % probability on 29 °C and 36 % on 30 °C, aligns with model guidance showing limited cloud cover and no strong frontal systems to suppress insolation or enhance mixing. Historical August climatology for southern Bavaria supports occasional 29–30 °C days when high pressure dominates, while the low odds on extremes above 31 °C or below 27 °C reflect the narrow uncertainty range typical one day ahead of resolution. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will refine the final observed high before markets settle.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble model consensus point to a highest temperature of 22–23°C in London on August 20, as an unsettled Atlantic flow brings patchy rain and increased cloud cover that limits daytime heating. With the date only two days ahead, short-range forecasts show modest afternoon maxima near or slightly above the long-term August average of roughly 21–22°C, with showers and variable winds preventing stronger warming. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to these outcomes because model runs continue to favor limited insolation and modest thermal advection rather than clear, anticyclonic conditions that could push readings toward 24–25°C. Minor shifts in the timing or intensity of rain bands remain the main source of uncertainty ahead of the next forecast updates.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble model consensus indicate a mostly cloudy day with scattered showers for Tokyo on August 20, supporting maximum temperatures near 32–33°C and limiting surface heating. Mid-August climatology shows a long-term average high of about 31°C, but elevated humidity and reduced solar insolation from cloud cover are capping extremes below 34°C while steering patterns and residual monsoon moisture suppress cooler outcomes. Short-term model runs exhibit limited spread, with urban heat-island effects and boundary-layer conditions reinforcing the current trader weighting toward 31–32°C as the most probable resolution range ahead of peak afternoon heating.

This range reflects typical late-summer high-pressure patterns that suppress cloud cover and allow modest warming above the long-term August average high near 22–23°C, without the stronger advection or subsidence needed for 30°C or higher. Recent model runs show limited spread, supporting the combined 79% trader consensus on 28–29°C while assigning only modest odds to 30°C. Updated guidance closer to the daily peak will refine these values, as small shifts in cloud timing or boundary-layer mixing can alter the observed high by 1–2°C.
